headline: Investor David Sacks pushed back on Bill Gates's warning that AI could cause a billion deaths, asking how any US rules could stop Chinese AI models.
score_reason: The exchange took place on 1 Oct, before 4 Oct, and is mostly social media posts; lowered by 2.
importance_line: It matters to lawmakers weighing mandatory AI law and to the public hearing extreme death-toll claims, but 24/7 Wall St. itself says no law moves and no new facts are offered.
source: 24/7 Wall St., citing NBC's Meet the Press and posts on X
summary: 24/7 Wall St. reports that David Sacks, a venture capitalist who stepped down as White House AI czar in the spring, answered Bill Gates on X on 1 Oct 2026. Gates said on NBC's Meet the Press, in an interview aired Sunday 27 Sep, that AI is "certainly powerful enough to drive events that cause a billion deaths" and urged Congress to pass mandatory federal law; Sacks reposted clips saying there is "no facts or evidence" for such numbers and asked how Gates would stop Chinese models from developing these capabilities.
notes: REPLY STORY: Sacks answers Gates's Meet the Press remarks (aired 27 Sep 2026, NBC). Whether we carried either earlier is not known to this writer, so the summary names the original report and its date rather than 'in our edition'. The article is an investor-oriented piece with market commentary on Alphabet, left out.
